description.en: Ismail I was proclaimed shah at Tabriz in 1501 and made Twelver Shi'ism the state religion. The Safavids lost to the Ottomans at Chaldiran, moved the capital to Isfahan under Abbas I, and lost Isfahan to Afghan forces in 1722.
description.es: Ismail I fue proclamado sah en Tabriz en 1501 e hizo del chiismo duodecimano la religión de Estado. Los safávidas perdieron ante los otomanos en Chaldirán, trasladaron la capital a Isfahán con Abás I y perdieron Isfahán ante fuerzas afganas en 1722.
description.zh: 伊斯迈尔一世于1501年在大不里士被拥立为沙阿，并以十二伊玛目派什叶派为国教。萨非王朝在恰尔迪兰败于奥斯曼人，阿拔斯一世时迁都伊斯法罕，1722年伊斯法罕被阿富汗军队攻占。

sources.citation: British Museum collection thesaurus, "Safavid dynasty" (1501–1722), via PeriodO.
Wikidata, "Safavid Iran" (Q18234383): start 1501, end 8 March 1736.
Library of Congress Country Studies, "Iran: The Safavids, 1501–1722".

note.en: Afghan forces took Isfahan in 1722, which ends the dynasty in the British Museum's dating. Safavid princes still held the throne in name until Nader Shah took it in 1736, the end date Wikidata uses.
note.es: Fuerzas afganas tomaron Isfahán en 1722, lo que cierra la dinastía en la cronología del Museo Británico. Príncipes safávidas siguieron en el trono nominalmente hasta que Nader Sah lo tomó en 1736, la fecha final que usa Wikidata.
note.zh: 1722年阿富汗军队攻占伊斯法罕，大英博物馆的断代即以此为王朝终点。萨非王室成员名义上仍在位，直到1736年纳迪尔沙夺取王位，这是维基数据采用的终点。

title.en: Ismail I is proclaimed shah at Tabriz and makes Twelver Shi'ism the state religion
title.es: Ismail I es proclamado sah en Tabriz y hace del chiismo duodecimano la religión de Estado
title.zh: 伊斯迈尔一世在大不里士被拥立为沙阿，并定十二伊玛目派什叶派为国教

sources.citation: Encyclopedia.com, "Isma'il I, Shah (1487–1524)": crowned at Tabriz in 1501; established Twelver Shi'ism as the official state religion.
EBSCO Research Starters, "Isma'il I": coronation in Tabriz in 1501; Shia Islam the state religion.
U.S. Library of Congress Country Studies, "Iran: The Safavids, 1501-1722" (the Safavids seize power in Tabriz in 1501 and declare Shia Islam the state religion).

title.en: The Ottoman sultan Selim I defeats Ismail I at Chaldiran and briefly occupies Tabriz
title.es: El sultán otomano Selim I derrota a Ismail I en Chaldirán y ocupa brevemente Tabriz
title.zh: 奥斯曼苏丹塞利姆一世在恰尔迪兰击败伊斯迈尔一世，并短暂占领大不里士

sources.citation: EBSCO Research Starters, "Reign of Selim I": Ottoman victory at Chaldiran on 23 August 1514; Selim captured Tabriz for a time.
World History Encyclopedia, "Battles & Conquests of the Ottoman Empire (1299-1683)": Selim defeats the Shah at Chaldiran in 1514, takes Tabriz, then retreats.

title.en: Maqsud Kashani oversees the Ardabil Carpet, the world's oldest dated carpet, believed to be made for the Safavid family shrine
title.es: Maqsud Kashani dirige la Alfombra de Ardabil, la alfombra fechada más antigua del mundo, que se cree hecha para el santuario de la familia safávida
title.zh: 马克苏德·卡尚尼主持织造阿尔达比勒地毯，这是世界上最古老的有纪年地毯，据信为萨非王室的家族圣陵而作

sources.citation: Victoria and Albert Museum, "The Ardabil Carpet": the world's oldest dated carpet; signed by Maqsud Kashani and dated A.H. 946 (1539–40); believed commissioned for the shrine of Shaykh Safi.
Los Angeles County Museum of Art, "Maqsud Kashani, Ardabil Carpet, dated 1539–40 (A.H. 946)": a matched pair with the V&A carpet; place made Iran, possibly Tabriz.

note.en: The carpet is dated A.H. 946, which spans 1539 and 1540. It was woven as one of a matched pair, now split between the V&A and LACMA. LACMA says it was possibly made in Tabriz.
note.es: La alfombra está fechada en el año 946 de la hégira, que abarca 1539 y 1540. Se tejió como una de un par, hoy repartido entre el V&A y el LACMA. El LACMA dice que posiblemente se hizo en Tabriz.
note.zh: 地毯的纪年为伊斯兰历946年，横跨1539年和1540年。它是成对织造的两张之一，如今分藏于维多利亚与阿尔伯特博物馆和洛杉矶郡立艺术博物馆。洛杉矶郡立艺术博物馆称其可能织于大不里士。

title.en: Abbas I moves the capital from Qazvin to Isfahan and builds a new city beside the old one
title.es: Abás I traslada la capital de Qazvin a Isfahán y construye una ciudad nueva junto a la antigua
title.zh: 阿拔斯一世把都城从加兹温迁到伊斯法罕，并在旧城旁兴建新城

sources.citation: EBSCO Research Starters, "Reign of 'Abbas the Great": Abbas moved the capital from Qazvin to Isfahan in 1598.
Encyclopedia.com, "Empires: Safavid and Qajar": capital transferred from Qazvin to Isfahan in the 1590s; Isfahan given a newly built administrative and commercial center.
Encyclopedia.com, "Abbas I": under Shah Abbas, Isfahan became Iran's capital, with a new center around a great square.

note.en: EBSCO gives 1598 for the move from Qazvin; Encyclopedia.com says only the 1590s. The date is given here as 1597 to 1598 to cover both.
note.es: EBSCO da 1598 para el traslado desde Qazvin; Encyclopedia.com dice solo la década de 1590. Aquí se da 1597 a 1598 para cubrir ambas.
note.zh: EBSCO 把由加兹温迁都定在1598年；Encyclopedia.com 只说在1590年代。这里写作1597至1598年以涵盖两种说法。

title.en: Safavid forces, with English help, take Hormuz from the Portuguese
title.es: Las fuerzas safávidas, con ayuda inglesa, toman Ormuz a los portugueses
title.zh: 萨非军队在英国人协助下从葡萄牙人手中夺取霍尔木兹

sources.citation: EBSCO Research Starters, "Reign of 'Abbas the Great": Portuguese control of Hormuz removed in 1622 with British East India Company naval aid.
World History Encyclopedia, "Estado da India": the Persians, with English assistance, took over Hormuz in 1622.
U.S. Library of Congress Country Studies, "Iran: The Safavids, 1501-1722" (Shah Abbas uses the British to expel the Portuguese from Hormoz in 1623).

note.en: World History Encyclopedia and EBSCO date the fall of Hormuz to 1622; the Library of Congress study says 1623. One World History Encyclopedia article calls the attackers Arabs; the other, and EBSCO, give the Persians with English naval help.
note.es: La World History Encyclopedia y EBSCO fechan la caída de Ormuz en 1622; el estudio de la Biblioteca del Congreso dice 1623. Un artículo de la World History Encyclopedia llama árabes a los atacantes; el otro, y EBSCO, hablan de los persas con ayuda naval inglesa.
note.zh: 世界历史百科和 EBSCO 把霍尔木兹陷落定在1622年；美国国会图书馆的研究作1623年。世界历史百科有一篇文章称进攻者为阿拉伯人；另一篇和 EBSCO 则说是波斯人，得到英国海军协助。

title.en: Afghan Ghilzai forces take Isfahan, ending effective Safavid rule
title.es: Las fuerzas afganas ghilzai toman Isfahán y ponen fin al dominio safávida efectivo
title.zh: 阿富汗吉尔扎伊军队攻占伊斯法罕，萨非王朝实际统治终结

sources.citation: EBSCO Research Starters, "Persian-Afghan Wars": Mahmud Ghilzai besieges Isfahan in 1722, leading to the abdication of the last Safavid ruler, Husayn I.
U.S. Library of Congress Country Studies, "Iran: The Safavids, 1501-1722" (Afghan forces take Isfahan in 1722).
U.S. Library of Congress Country Studies, "Afghanistan: Mughal-Safavid Rivalry, ca. 1500–1747".

title.en: Tahmasp Quli, who had ruled in the name of a Safavid prince, takes power in his own name as Nader Shah
title.es: Tahmasp Quli, que gobernaba en nombre de un príncipe safávida, toma el poder en nombre propio como Nader Sah
title.zh: 此前以萨非王室成员之名执政的塔赫马斯普·库利，改以纳迪尔沙之名亲自掌权

sources.citation: U.S. Library of Congress Country Studies, "Iran: The Safavids, 1501-1722" (Tahmasp Quli expels the Afghans in the name of a Safavid and in 1736 assumes power in his own name as Nader Shah).
EBSCO Research Starters, "Persian-Afghan Wars": Nader Shah formally takes the throne in 1736.
Wikidata, "Safavid Iran" (Q18234383): dissolved 8 March 1736.

text.en: Ismail I's Turkmen soldiers were called Qizilbash, "red heads", after their red caps.
text.es: Los soldados turcomanos de Ismail I se llamaban qizilbash, "cabezas rojas", por sus gorros rojos.
text.zh: 伊斯迈尔一世麾下的突厥语部落士兵因戴红帽而被称为“红头”（克孜勒巴什）。

sources.citation: Encyclopedia.com, "Empires: Safavid and Qajar": the Qizilbash, "redheads" from their red headgear, were the mainstay of the Safavid army.
U.S. Library of Congress Country Studies, "Iran: The Safavids, 1501-1722" (the qizilbash fighting forces came from the Turkic-speaking tribes behind the Safavid bid for power).
